papers.title: Hybrid CNN and multi-head attention model for analyzing epigenetic mechanisms and gene expression across fungal phylogenetic distances.
papers.abstract: Understanding gene expression is crucial for optimizing biological processes in bioeconomic processes, human health, and environmental regulation. Epigenetic modifications significantly influence gene expression by altering chromatin structure and DNA accessibility. However, knowledge about the conservation of these mechanisms across species, especially in non-model organisms, is limited. This study predicts gene expression levels based on epigenetic modifications across fungal species, facilitating knowledge transfer from well-characterized to less understood species. We developed a deep lear
papers.summary: This study presents a deep learning model combining convolutional neural networks and multi-head attention to predict gene expression from epigenetic modifications across fungal species. The model enables knowledge transfer from well-characterized to less-studied species, addressing the limited understanding of epigenetic mechanism conservation in non-model organisms.

papers.title: Protocol for haplotype-resolved structural variant detection via long-read sequencing using cuteHap.
papers.abstract: Long-read sequencing technologies have revolutionized human genome exploration at an unparalleled resolution, particularly facilitating the analysis of structural variation (SV) at haplotype resolution. Here, we present a protocol for using cuteHap, a robust framework for haplotype-aware SV detection through phased alignment reads generated by diverse long-read sequencing platforms. We describe procedures for single-nucleotide variant (SNV) calling, read phasing, SV calling, and genotyping. We also establish a benchmarking pipeline to evaluate the detected SV callsets. For complete details on
papers.summary: This protocol paper describes cuteHap, a framework for haplotype-resolved structural variant (SV) detection using long-read sequencing data. It provides step-by-step procedures for SNV calling, read phasing, SV calling, and genotyping, along with a benchmarking pipeline to evaluate SV callsets. The protocol enables researchers to leverage long-read data for more accurate, haplotype-aware SV analysis.

papers.title: Minimal organism JCVI-syn3.0, an engineered derivative of Mycoplasma mycoides, encodes an assortment of unrecognized membrane transporters and immunity factors.
papers.abstract: In 2016, researchers at the J. Craig Venter Institute produced JCVI-Syn3.0, a derivative of Mycoplasma mycoides subsp. capri Large Colony strain GM12 with a re-engineered, minimized genome. The minimal synthetic genome of 532 kbp encodes 473 genes, selected from ∼910 parent genes on the basis of their indispensability, that is, a lethal phenotype caused by a knockout of each such gene. Among these genes, 438 genes encode proteins, of which ∼150 were not assigned a molecular function or predicted cellular role. A decade later, despite community annotation efforts, 50-60 of these putative protei
papers.summary: This study re-analyzes the minimal genome of JCVI-syn3.0 and identifies previously uncharacterized membrane transporters and immunity factors, suggesting that even the simplest synthetic organism harbors functional complexity beyond initial annotations. The findings highlight the value of deep functional curation for minimal genomes and may inform future synthetic biology designs.

papers.title: Genetic variation in oxidative stress and detoxification pathways associated with prostate cancer susceptibility: a pathway-based analysis.
papers.abstract: Redox imbalance and impaired detoxification pathways have been implicated in prostate carcinogenesis; however, the specific genetic variants that modulate these processes remain insufficiently characterized. We used a two-stage, pathway-focused design in which PRACTICAL consortium meta-GWAS summary statistics (79,148 cases and 61,106 controls) were used for initial gene-level prioritization, whereas formal variant-level effect estimation was based on FinnGen and UK Biobank summary statistics (19,209 cases and 288,847 controls). PRACTICAL was not included in the formal variant-level meta-analys
papers.summary: This study investigated genetic variants in oxidative stress and detoxification pathways linked to prostate cancer risk using a two-stage, pathway-focused analysis of large GWAS datasets. It identified specific genes and variants in these pathways that may modulate prostate cancer susceptibility, providing new insights into the genetic architecture of the disease.

papers.title: Carbon substrate type shapes spatial self-organization in a multi-species biofilm community.
papers.abstract: Spatial organization is a defining feature of multispecies biofilms and critically influences microbial interactions and emergent community properties. However, understanding and manipulating how microbes assemble into spatially structured biofilms remains challenging because most experimental frameworks emphasize species composition and pairwise interactions, while often overlooking the spatial constraints on biofilms imposed by the environment. In this study, we focus on how carbon substrate type, distinguishing between diffusible sugars and polymeric substrates, affects biofilm self-organiz
papers.summary: This study investigates how the type of carbon substrate—diffusible sugars versus polymeric substrates—affects the spatial self-organization of multispecies biofilms. The findings reveal that substrate type is a key environmental factor shaping biofilm architecture, which has implications for understanding and manipulating microbial community assembly.

papers.title: nf-core/pacsomatic: a scalable somatic analytic pipeline using PacBio HiFi data.
papers.abstract: Pacific Biosciences (PacBio) HiFi long-read sequencing enables robust characterization of complex genomic regions, repetitive elements, and structural variants (SVs) that are often inaccessible to short-read technologies. To fully leverage HiFi reads to advance cancer genomics and epigenetics, researchers require an end-to-end, scalable and optimized bioinformatics workflow. The nf-core framework meets this need by providing rigorously tested, community-curated pipelines that ensure reproducibility, transparency, and broad compatibility across computational environments.
papers.summary: This paper introduces nf-core/pacsomatic, a scalable and reproducible bioinformatics pipeline for analyzing PacBio HiFi long-read sequencing data in cancer genomics. It provides an end-to-end workflow for characterizing complex genomic regions, structural variants, and epigenetic features that are often missed by short-read technologies.

papers.title: Variant calling in non-model organisms with snpArcher.
papers.abstract: Population genomic studies in non-model organisms increasingly depend on whole-genome resequencing, yet translating raw reads into reliable variant callsets remains a practical challenge due to the complexity of multi-step bioinformatics pipelines and the absence of species-specific best practices. Here we present a step-by-step protocol for snpArcher, a Snakemake-based workflow that takes raw sequencing reads and a reference genome as input and produces a filtered, joint-called VCF suitable for downstream population genomic analysis. We guide users through six phases: installation and environ
papers.summary: This paper presents a step-by-step protocol for snpArcher, a Snakemake-based workflow that simplifies variant calling in non-model organisms by taking raw sequencing reads and a reference genome to produce a filtered, joint-called VCF. It addresses the practical challenges of multi-step bioinformatics pipelines and provides guidance for researchers without species-specific best practices.

papers.title: Computational Pipeline Reveals Nature's Untapped Reservoir of Halogenating Enzymes.
papers.abstract: Microbial halogenated natural products (hNPs) hold ecological, agricultural, and biomedical relevance. The hNP-producing potential of an organism can be assessed by the precise prediction of halogenating enzymes, yet detailed annotations of halogenases are often missing from genomic and metagenomic data. We created a manually curated database (https://halogenases.secondarymetabolites.org/) containing information on the halide specificity, role, and position of verified catalytic residues and the results of mutagenesis studies of more than 120 experimentally validated or in silico inferred halo
papers.summary: The authors developed a computational pipeline and manually curated database of halogenating enzymes, enabling precise prediction of halogenase function from genomic and metagenomic data. This resource reveals a vast, previously untapped reservoir of halogenating enzymes in nature, with potential applications in ecology, agriculture, and drug discovery.

papers.title: SNPannotator: Automated Functional Annotation of Genetic Variants and Linked Proxies.
papers.abstract: Genome-wide association studies (GWASs) have identified thousands of genetic variants associated with complex traits and diseases. However, explaining the mechanisms underlying phenotypic variation remains challenging. Here, we introduce SNPannotator, an automated post-GWAS analysis software package designed to streamline the interpretation of GWAS findings. Our pipeline implements a multi-step process that identifies proxy variants in high linkage disequilibrium (LD) with associated lead variants, then queries comprehensive resources (including Ensembl, the GTEx Portal, the eQTL Catalog, and
papers.summary: SNPannotator is a new automated software pipeline that streamlines post-GWAS analysis by identifying proxy variants in linkage disequilibrium and querying multiple functional databases (Ensembl, GTEx, eQTL Catalog) to annotate genetic variants. This tool aims to help researchers interpret the functional mechanisms underlying GWAS-associated variants more efficiently.

papers.title: Ion chromatography-ultra-high-resolution mass spectrometry reveals EZH2-driven reprogramming of nucleic acid and protein methylation.
papers.abstract: ENHANCER OF ZESTE: homolog 2 (EZH2), a histone H3K27 trimethyltransferase, is a key epigenetic regulator frequently dysregulated in cancer. To determine its impact on nucleotide biosynthesis and nucleic acid methylation in intact cells requires highly sensitive, isomer-resolving analytical workflows. We developed a targeted ion chromatography-ultra-high-resolution Fourier transform mass spectrometry (IC-UHR-FTMS) workflow with lower limits of quantification down to 9 fmol on-column to determine changes in methylation of DNA, total RNA, and mRNA in A549 cells following EZH2 knockdown (KD). Usin
papers.summary: This paper presents a new ion chromatography-ultra-high-resolution mass spectrometry (IC-UHR-FTMS) workflow that can quantify nucleic acid and protein methylation with high sensitivity (down to 9 fmol). Using this method, the authors show that EZH2 knockdown in A549 cells reprograms methylation patterns in DNA, RNA, and proteins, revealing a broader role for EZH2 beyond histone modification.

papers.title: Natural Infection of Domestic Dogs with Raccoon Dog and Fox Amdoparvovirus During a Severe Disease Outbreak.
papers.abstract: Raccoon dog and fox amdoparvovirus (RFAV) has been reported in raccoon dogs and foxes, but natural infection in domestic dogs has not previously been documented. During March-April 2026, samples from four affected Dobermann dogs from a kennel near Novi Sad, Serbia, were submitted for laboratory investigation. After negative testing for canine adenovirus, canine coronavirus, herpesvirus, parvovirus, distemper virus, influenza A virus, and leptospirosis, metagenomic sequencing was performed on selected tissues, followed by bioinformatic analysis and targeted RFAV PCR screening of additional outb
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This study documents the first natural infection of domestic dogs with raccoon dog and fox amdoparvovirus (RFAV), identified via metagenomic sequencing during a severe disease outbreak in a Serbian kennel. The findings expand the known host range of RFAV and highlight the utility of unbiased sequencing for diagnosing unusual pathogens in domestic animals.

papers.title: ESM2-Guided Context-Aware Annotation Completion Supplements Carbohydrate Metabolism Coverage in Silage Microbial Metagenomes.
papers.abstract: Functional annotation gaps limit the interpretation of carbohydrate metabolism in silage microbiomes. We developed Context-Aware Annotation Completion (CAAC), a framework integrating ESM2 embeddings, genomic-neighborhood features, three-class classification, confidence-tiered neighbor voting, and Enzyme Commission (EC)-to-KEGG Orthology (KO) mapping. CAAC was applied to 21 metagenomes from uninoculated and Lacticaseibacillus paracasei-inoculated silages sampled before ensiling and at 7 and 90 days. Five-fold cross-validation yielded an F1-macro of 84.64% for negative, positive, and hard-sequen
papers.summary: The authors developed CAAC, a framework that uses ESM2 protein embeddings and genomic context to predict missing functional annotations for carbohydrate metabolism genes in silage metagenomes. Applied to 21 silage samples, it achieved high cross-validation performance and improved annotation coverage, enabling better interpretation of microbial carbohydrate metabolism.

papers.title: Identification of DNA-Binding Factor Enrichment in Chromatin Accessibility Data to Define a Persister Cell Signature.
papers.abstract: Chemotherapy-resistant persister cells are a major driver of cancer recurrence, yet their epigenetic basis remains poorly characterized. This protocol describes a computational pipeline for identifying DNA-binding factors (DBFs) that are enriched in accessible chromatin that collectively define a persister cell signature (PCS). Starting from single-nucleus ATAC-seq (snATAC-seq) data processed through the 10x Genomics CellRanger ARC pipeline, this protocol covers (1) the creation of a Seurat/Signac object with ATAC peaks, (2) the optional integration of DNA-binding data from the ReMap2022 datab
papers.summary: This protocol paper describes a computational pipeline for analyzing single-nucleus ATAC-seq data to identify DNA-binding factors enriched in accessible chromatin regions, which together define a persister cell signature in chemotherapy-resistant cancer cells. The pipeline integrates snATAC-seq data with DNA-binding data from the ReMap2022 database, using Seurat/Signac for processing, and provides a step-by-step approach for researchers to apply this analysis to their own data.

papers.title: Integrative GWAS Catalog Analysis of Proxy-Trait Intersection in Sarcopenia-Related Musculoskeletal Aging with Multi-Criteria Evidence Integration.
papers.abstract: Sarcopenia is a multidimensional musculoskeletal-aging phenotype defined by reduced muscle quantity together with weakness and impaired performance, but public genetic resources rarely capture sarcopenia as a single uniformly labeled phenotype.
papers.summary: This paper presents an integrative analysis of GWAS catalog data to study sarcopenia by combining proxy traits like muscle mass, strength, and physical performance. It uses multi-criteria evidence integration to identify genetic loci and pathways relevant to musculoskeletal aging, addressing the challenge that sarcopenia is not uniformly defined in public genetic resources.

papers.title: Structural Variation and Its Roles in Plant Genomes.
papers.abstract: Plant genomes exhibit extensive structural diversity generated by large-scale genomic alterations, collectively known as structural variations (SVs). Unlike single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and small insertions/deletions (indels), SVs can reshape genome architecture through changes in sequence content, gene dosage, regulatory landscapes, and chromosome organization. Recent advances in long-read sequencing (LRS), pan-genome construction, and multi-omics technologies have greatly expanded our ability to identify and interpret SVs across plant species. In this review, we summarize recent pr
papers.summary: This review discusses the role of structural variations (SVs) in plant genomes, highlighting how they differ from SNPs and indels by reshaping genome architecture, gene dosage, and regulatory landscapes. It emphasizes recent advances in long-read sequencing and pan-genome construction that have improved SV identification and interpretation across plant species.

papers.title: Molecular Characterization of Endometrial Cancer Using a Laboratory-Developed Multi-Gene NGS Panel.
papers.abstract: Endometrial carcinoma is a biologically and clinically heterogeneous neoplasm, for which molecular classification now plays a central role in determining prognosis and guiding treatment. The aim of this study was to develop and apply an in-house multi-gene NGS panel to expand the molecular characterization of endometrial tumors beyond the markers required for surrogate classification. Seventy primary endometrial carcinomas were selected and analyzed by immunohistochemistry for p53, mismatch repair proteins, ARID1A, and PTEN, and by NGS on DNA extracted from FFPE samples using a panel comprisin
papers.summary: This study describes the development and application of an in-house multi-gene NGS panel to characterize endometrial tumors beyond standard surrogate markers. Analysis of 70 primary endometrial carcinomas by immunohistochemistry and NGS on FFPE samples demonstrates the panel's utility in expanding molecular profiling for this cancer type.

papers.title: Computational Genomics for Resistome Characterization: Current Advancements and Future Challenges Under a One Health Perspective.
papers.abstract: The resistome, defined as the complete set of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) present in the microbiota of a given environment, is a critical component for understanding the evolutionary dynamics of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and its impact on human, animal, and environmental health. This review summarizes current methods and technological advances and offers a forward-looking perspective on resistome research. A systematic literature search was conducted. References on short-read and long-read sequencing, amplicon sequencing, shotgun metagenomics, and multi-omics integration were inclu
papers.summary: This review summarizes current computational methods and technological advances for characterizing the resistome—the collection of antibiotic resistance genes in a microbiome—using sequencing and multi-omics approaches. It highlights the importance of a One Health perspective and discusses future challenges in understanding antimicrobial resistance across human, animal, and environmental health.

papers.title: AI-Assisted Cross-Study Synthesis in Genome Editing: Comparing Long-Context Strategies and Uncovering Latent Contradictions in the CRISPR-Cas9 Guide RNA Prediction Literature.
papers.abstract: Predicting CRISPR-Cas9 guide RNA efficiency and off-target activity is a precondition for precise genome editing. Computational models have progressively incorporated chromatin accessibility and epigenetic descriptors into their feature sets, yet synthesising findings from independently published studies-especially when those studies contradict one another-remains an unresolved methodological gap. Large Language Models (LLMs) have been proposed as a route to automate cross-study synthesis, but their utility depends on a constraint that receives less attention than model architecture: how much
papers.summary: This study evaluates the use of large language models (LLMs) to synthesize findings from CRISPR-Cas9 guide RNA prediction studies, focusing on how different long-context strategies handle contradictory results across publications. The authors uncover latent contradictions in the literature and demonstrate that the choice of context window strategy significantly impacts the quality of AI-assisted synthesis, highlighting a methodological gap in automated cross-study analysis.

papers.title: DNA methylation profiling enables subclassification of mucinous ovarian carcinoma and distinguishes it from extraovarian mucinous metastases.
papers.abstract: Mucinous ovarian carcinoma (MOC) is an epithelial ovarian cancer subtype that is frequently misclassified as extraovarian mucinous metastasis (EOM) because of overlapping features. To address this diagnostic challenge, we perform genome-wide DNA methylation profiling of 58 MOCs, 38 EOMs, and 18 mucinous borderline ovarian tumors (mBOTs) collected from six institutions. Methylation analysis defines two mBOT groups, one epigenetically similar to normal ovary and one resembling MOC. Unsupervised clustering reveals two distinct MOC methylation subtypes with potential prognostic relevance in the in
papers.summary: This study uses genome-wide DNA methylation profiling to distinguish mucinous ovarian carcinoma (MOC) from extraovarian mucinous metastases (EOM), which are often misdiagnosed due to overlapping features. The analysis identifies two distinct MOC methylation subtypes with potential prognostic relevance, and also defines two groups of mucinous borderline ovarian tumors, one resembling normal ovary and one resembling MOC. These findings provide a potential epigenetic classifier to improve diagnostic accuracy and may inform prognosis.

papers.title: The LncRNA-Tumor Immune Microenvironment Nexus: Integrative Insights for Cancer Immunotherapy.
papers.abstract: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) have emerged as pivotal regulators of tumor-immune interactions, bridging epigenetic, transcriptional, and post-transcriptional control of immune signaling networks. Recent multi-omics analyses reveal that lncRNAs shape the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) by influencing immune-cell differentiation, activation, and exhaustion, as well as cytokine, chemokine, and immune-checkpoint pathways. Acting through molecular scaffolding, chromatin remodeling, and competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) mechanisms, lncRNAs orchestrate the recruitment and functional polarization
papers.summary: This review synthesizes recent multi-omics findings on how long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) regulate the tumor immune microenvironment, influencing immune cell behavior and checkpoint pathways. It highlights the potential of lncRNAs as biomarkers and therapeutic targets in cancer immunotherapy.

papers.title: Integrated proteomic, transcriptomic, and epigenomic profiling identifies SRA1 as a novel therapeutic target for postpartum depression.
papers.abstract: Postpartum depression (PPD) is among the most common complications of childbirth, and identifying novel treatments is vital. We aimed to identify potential drug targets for PPD by integrating the plasma proteome, transcriptome and epigenome. We designed a comprehensive analysis pipeline involving two-sample Mendelian randomisation (MR) (for proteins), colocalisation (for coding genes), and summary-based MR (SMR) (for mRNA and DNA methylation) to identify potential therapeutic targets for PPD. Genetic data on the plasma proteome were obtained from 4907 aptamers in 35,559 Icelanders and 7596 pro
papers.summary: This study integrates plasma proteomic, transcriptomic, and epigenomic data using Mendelian randomization and colocalization analyses to identify SRA1 as a potential novel therapeutic target for postpartum depression. The findings suggest that targeting SRA1 could offer a new treatment avenue for PPD.

papers.title: Decitabine Reprograms Temozolomide-Resistant Glioblastoma Through Epigenetic Reactivation and Mesenchymal Attenuation: A Multi-Omics Study.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most lethal primary brain malignancy in adults, with a median overall survival of approximately 15 months. Temozolomide (TMZ) resistance develops in virtually all patients, and no second-line regimen has improved outcomes over the past two decades. The DNA methyltransferase inhibitor decitabine (DAC) has attracted interest as a chemosensitizer, but whether it directly reverses the TMZ-resistance transcriptome or operates through distinct, complementary mechanisms has not been tested at multi-omics resolution. Methods: We performed an integrative
papers.summary: This study uses a multi-omics approach to investigate how the DNA methyltransferase inhibitor decitabine (DAC) affects temozolomide-resistant glioblastoma cells. The findings suggest that DAC reprograms the resistant cells through epigenetic reactivation and attenuation of the mesenchymal phenotype, potentially offering a complementary strategy to overcome chemoresistance.

papers.title: Deep learning enabled prediction of nuclear lamina-associated chromatin.
papers.abstract: Tethering of chromatin regions to the nuclear lamina contributes to genome organization and gene regulation. Though several molecular and epigenomic determinants of lamina association have been studied, the influence of genomic sequences has received less attention. Here, we present lamina-associated domain finder (LADDER), a multimodal deep learning model to predict lamina association based on DNA sequence, gene density, and long interspersed nuclear element (LINE)1 and short interspersed nuclear element (SINE) densities. The predictions made by LADDER are cell-type independent. Using LADDER'
papers.summary: The authors introduce LADDER, a multimodal deep learning model that predicts nuclear lamina-associated chromatin domains from DNA sequence, gene density, and repeat element (LINE1/SINE) densities, independent of cell type. This work highlights the role of genomic sequence features in determining lamina association and provides a new predictive tool for studying genome organization.

papers.title: Genome-Wide and GWAS Dissection of Maize Fibrillin Genes Reveals Plastid Regulators of Drought and Salt Stress Tolerance.
papers.abstract: Fibrillins (FBNs) are conserved plastid-associated proteins implicated in plant development and abiotic stress responses; however, their roles in maize remain unclear. In this study, through a genome-wide bioinformatic analysis, we identified 14 ZmFBN genes in the maize genome and characterized their phylogeny, chromosomal distribution, gene structure, conserved motifs, and promoter cis-elements. ZmFBN members were grouped into several subfamilies that all retain a conserved PAP_fibrillin domain, whereas the variation in exon-intron organization, motif composition, and regulatory elements sugg
papers.summary: This study identifies and characterizes 14 fibrillin (ZmFBN) genes in the maize genome, revealing their evolutionary relationships, gene structures, and regulatory elements. Through GWAS, it links specific ZmFBN genes to drought and salt stress tolerance, suggesting they act as plastid regulators of abiotic stress responses in maize.

papers.title: Comprehensive Proteomic Profiling of Alternaria gansuense Provides Insights into Candidate Virulence-Associated Proteins and Core Physiological Features.
papers.abstract: Although Alternaria gansuense causes yellow stunt and root rot (YSRR)-a destructive disease of the leguminous forage Astragalus adsurgens in northern China-systematic investigations of this pathogen at the protein level remain scarce. In this study, we establish an optimized proteomic workflow for A. gansuense by comparing two protein extraction methods. Using data-independent acquisition (DIA) mass spectrometry with a DIA-NN search against the Alternaria protein database, we construct the first comprehensive proteome reference map of A. gansuense, then perform functional annotation via Gene O
papers.summary: This study presents the first comprehensive proteome reference map of the plant pathogen Alternaria gansuense, which causes yellow stunt and root rot in a leguminous forage crop. By optimizing protein extraction and using DIA mass spectrometry, the authors identified candidate virulence-associated proteins and core physiological features, providing a foundational resource for understanding this pathogen's biology and pathogenicity.

papers.title: Genetic Findings in Seven Cochlear Implanted Patients with Severe-to-Profound Hearing Loss.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Hearing loss is one of the most prevalent sensory disorders in humans, with genetic factors accounting for approximately 60% of cases. Cochlear implantation is an effective intervention for individuals with severe-to-profound hearing loss. However, substantial variability in postoperative auditory performance persists, complicating the prediction of individual outcomes. This study investigated the genetic findings associated with hearing loss in a cohort of seven affected adults with cochlear implants (CIs). Methods: A total of seven patients with severe-to-profound hear
papers.summary: This study reports genetic findings from seven adult cochlear implant recipients with severe-to-profound hearing loss, identifying potential genetic causes and linking them to postoperative auditory outcomes. The results highlight the genetic heterogeneity of hearing loss and suggest that specific variants may influence cochlear implant performance, though the small cohort limits generalizability.

papers.title: Large-Scale Data Analysis of Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) Through GWAS Fine-Mapping and Systems Biology.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) is a complex psychiatric condition with a strong polygenic and stress-related biological basis. Although Genome-Wide Association Studies (GWAS) have acknowledged abundant risk variants, translating these findings into biologically meaningful candidates remains challenging. This study introduces an integrative computational approach from raw file preparation by python-coded application into downstream in-depth silico analyses designed to systematically refine GWAS signals for PTSD using fine-mapping, linkage disequilibrium (LD), and h
papers.summary: This study presents an integrative computational pipeline that combines GWAS fine-mapping, linkage disequilibrium analysis, and systems biology approaches to refine PTSD risk variants and identify biologically meaningful candidate genes. The approach aims to bridge the gap between statistical associations and functional understanding in PTSD genetics.

papers.title: Single cell CRISPR screen identifies antagonism between Nsd1-H3K36me2 and Ezh2-H3K27me3 orchestrates pluripotency transition.
papers.abstract: The transcriptional and epigenetic landscape imposes constraints on the self-renewal capacity and lineage specification potential of both naive and primed mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs). CRISPR/Cas9-based functional screening coupled with single-cell RNA-seq (CROP-seq) establishes relationships between gRNA-mediated knockout genotype and transcriptome phenotype, providing a powerful tool to dissect gene regulatory networks. Here, we employed CROP-seq to investigate the epigenetic regulation governing the pluripotency network in mESCs. This highly sensitive method identified key genes essen
papers.summary: This study uses CROP-seq, a single-cell CRISPR screen, to identify epigenetic regulators essential for the pluripotency transition in mouse embryonic stem cells. The screen reveals an antagonistic relationship between Nsd1-mediated H3K36me2 and Ezh2-mediated H3K27me3 that orchestrates the switch between naive and primed pluripotency states.

papers.title: Flype: Integrating Molecular and Pharmacogenomic Results to Enhance Oncology Patient Care in a Community-Based Academic Cancer Center.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: We describe how our in-house bioinformatics platform, Flype, has evolved from being a variant repository to an enterprise role as an electronic medical record (EMR) content provider, powering molecular pathology reporting, pharmacogenomics reporting, sending discrete data to our EMR, aggregating internal and external molecular test results and powering our molecular tumor board (MTB). Methods: In response to critical pain points, we developed Docket, a sample tracking system in Flype, which manages multiple individual in-house molecular tests for NGS assays, pharmacogeno
papers.summary: This paper describes the evolution of Flype, an in-house bioinformatics platform at a community-based academic cancer center, from a variant repository to an enterprise-level system that integrates molecular and pharmacogenomic results into clinical care. The platform now powers molecular pathology and pharmacogenomics reporting, sends discrete data to the electronic medical record, aggregates internal and external test results, and supports the molecular tumor board, with a new sample tracking system called Docket to manage multiple molecular tests. This work demonstrates a practical approach to integrating complex genomic data into routine oncology practice in a community setting.

papers.title: A chromosome-level genome assembly of Platycladus orientalis and comparative genomics reveal pivotal roles of transposable elements in gene duplication and pseudogenization across gymnosperm giga-genomes.
papers.abstract: Gymnosperms, particularly conifers, exhibit a high abundance of transposable elements (TEs) in their giga-scale genomes. TEs interact both antagonistically and cooperatively with the host genome, promoting structural and genetic innovations across evolutionary lineages. However, how TEs shape the coding space of gymnosperm genomes remains a key unresolved question. Here, we present a high-quality genome assembly for the keystone conifer Platycladus orientalis, with a contig N50 of 57.54 Mb-the highest continuity reported to date-to investigate the role of TEs. Comparative genomics confirms the
papers.summary: This study presents a high-quality chromosome-level genome assembly for Platycladus orientalis, achieving the highest contig continuity reported for a conifer, and uses comparative genomics to reveal that transposable elements have played pivotal roles in gene duplication and pseudogenization across gymnosperm giga-genomes.

papers.title: Integrative Epigenomics: Bioinformatics Strategies for Multi-Omics Data Analysis in Health and Disease.
papers.abstract: Background: Epigenomics has emerged as an essential field in modern molecular biology, providing a critical layer of gene regulation. DNA methylation, histone modifications and alterations to the chromatin accessibility of DNA have been widely associated with complex diseases including cancer. The most recent developments in high-throughput sequencing technology have made it possible to profile epigenetic landscapes genomically on a large scale. However, bulk averaging can obscure cellular heterogeneity essential for understanding complex disease states. The purpose of the review is to survey
papers.summary: This review surveys bioinformatics strategies for integrating multi-omics data in epigenomics, highlighting how high-throughput sequencing can profile epigenetic marks but noting that bulk averaging obscures cellular heterogeneity. It emphasizes the need for integrative approaches to understand complex diseases like cancer.

papers.title: ZATELLITE: a toolkit to visualize and manipulate human centromeres in live cells using synthetic zinc fingers.
papers.abstract: Changes in the number of chromosomes or their spatial organization within the nucleus have critical consequences for cell fate. Yet capturing the karyotype or three-dimensional architecture of chromatin in living cells remains limited by the difficulty in labeling endogenous loci non-invasively. The most widely used tools rely on dCas9, a bulky protein whose persistent DNA binding interferes with DNA and RNA metabolism, causes DNA damage, and is hard to multiplex. We developed ZATELLITE , an AI-enabled tool to target endogenous repetitive sequences with fluorescently-tagged synthetic zinc fing
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: ZATELLITE is a new toolkit that uses AI-designed synthetic zinc fingers to fluorescently label and manipulate human centromeres in live cells, offering a less invasive alternative to dCas9-based methods. This approach avoids the bulky dCas9 protein, reducing DNA damage and enabling better multiplexing for studying chromosome number and nuclear architecture in living cells.

papers.title: DNA Methylation Signatures of Upper Aerodigestive Tract Squamous Cell Carcinoma and Sarcomatoid Squamous Cell Carcinoma Are Similar: A Potential Novel Diagnostic Tool for the Diagnosis of Sarcomatoid Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Upper aerodigestive tract squamous cell carcinoma (UATSCC) is often easy to recognize in its conventional form. However, a subset of tumors loses histologic evidence of squamous differentiation and, instead, become sarcomatoid (spindled). These cases may be difficult or impossible to appropriately classify on biopsy material, even with immunohistochemistry. DNA methylation has emerged as a tool to help in classifying undifferentiated malignancies. We sought to explore whether conventional and sarcomatoid UATSCC harbor the same epigenetic signature.
papers.summary: This study investigated whether conventional and sarcomatoid (spindled) upper aerodigestive tract squamous cell carcinomas share similar DNA methylation profiles. The findings suggest that both forms have comparable epigenetic signatures, indicating that DNA methylation could serve as a diagnostic tool for challenging sarcomatoid cases where histology and immunohistochemistry are inconclusive.

papers.title: Methylation clocks fail to generalize across genetically admixed individuals.
papers.abstract: Epigenetic aging clocks based on DNA methylation patterns across the genome have emerged as a potential biomarker for risk of age-related diseases, like Alzheimer's disease (AD), and environmental and social stressors. However, methylation clocks have not been comprehensively validated in genetically diverse individuals. Here, we evaluate a set of first-, second-, and third-generation methylation clocks in 621 AD patients and matched controls from African American, Hispanic, and White cohorts. The clocks are less accurate at predicting age in genetically admixed cohorts compared to the White c
papers.summary: This study evaluates the accuracy of epigenetic aging clocks in genetically diverse cohorts and finds that they perform worse in genetically admixed individuals (African American and Hispanic) compared to White cohorts. The results highlight a critical limitation of current methylation clocks, which may bias age predictions and health risk assessments in non-European populations.

papers.title: Partial Reproducibility and Pleiotropic Epigenetic QTLs in Arabidopsis Recombinant Inbred Lines.
papers.abstract: Unlike conventional genetic polymorphisms, many induced epigenetic polymorphisms can be reset across generations, raising uncertainty about how consistently the same epigenetic loci and associated phenotypic effects can be recovered among independent studies. To address this problem, we designed our study specifically to maximize a lineage-matched, environmentally aligned cross-study comparability with the foundational work of Cortijo et al. by using seeds derived from the same epiRIL generation and grown under broadly similar environmental conditions. We mapped flowering time, as well as five
papers.summary: This study tests the reproducibility of epigenetic quantitative trait loci (epiQTLs) in Arabidopsis recombinant inbred lines, finding only partial overlap with a foundational study despite matched lineage and environment. The results reveal pleiotropic effects of epigenetic loci on flowering time and other traits, highlighting that while some epigenetic associations are stable, many are context-dependent and not fully reproducible across studies.

papers.title: Assessing the influence of different alignment tools on the accuracy of a forensic epigenetic clock.
papers.abstract: DNA methylation (DNAm) has long been a commonly investigated biomarker in biomedical research. The current gold standard for DNAm detection is bisulfite sequencing which requires dedicated alignment tools that can handle reduced sequence complexity. One commonly used application of DNAm are epigenetic clock measurements. These clocks have been adapted by many fields for their specific needs, including forensic genetics. Here, epigenetic clocks were designed to help estimate the chronological age of a biological stain donor for investigative purposes.
papers.summary: This study evaluates how different alignment tools affect the accuracy of a forensic epigenetic clock, which estimates a person's age from DNA methylation in biological stains. The authors find that the choice of alignment tool significantly impacts clock accuracy, highlighting the need for standardized pipelines in forensic applications.

papers.title: Conserved Core and Species-Specific Signatures in the Milk Exosomal microRNA Targetome: A Preliminary Comparative In Silico Analysis of Human, Cow, Goat and Donkey Milk.
papers.abstract: Milk-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) transport microRNAs (miRNAs) that are unusually stable and have been proposed to survive digestion and modulate gene expression in the consumer, although their dietary bioavailability and physiological relevance remain debated. How the predicted regulatory potential of these miRNAs differs among the milks of different animals most relevant to human nutrition has not been systematically compared. Here, we performed an integrative in silico analysis of publicly available small-RNA sequencing data from 29 milk and milk-cell samples of human, cow, goat, an
papers.summary: This study computationally compared the microRNA targetomes of milk-derived extracellular vesicles from human, cow, goat, and donkey, revealing conserved core regulatory targets as well as species-specific signatures. The findings suggest that while some miRNA-mediated effects may be shared across species, others are unique to each milk type, which could have implications for infant nutrition and the design of milk-based products.

papers.title: Absence of Germline BRCA1 and BRCA2 Copy Number Variations Among Breast Cancer Patients in the Three Southern Border Provinces of Thailand.
papers.abstract: The objective of this study is to investigate germline CNVs in the BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes.
papers.journal: Asian Pacific journal of cancer prevention : APJCP
papers.summary: This study investigated germline copy number variations (CNVs) in the BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes among breast cancer patients in the three southern border provinces of Thailand, finding no such CNVs in the studied cohort. The results suggest that CNVs in these genes are not a common cause of hereditary breast cancer in this specific population, highlighting the need for further genetic screening approaches.

papers.title: Quantitative comparison of fungal genome assembly strategies using short and long reads from simulated and empirical sequencing data.
papers.abstract: High-quality fungal reference genomes are essential for comparative, functional and evolutionary studies, yet fungal genome features such as repeats, structural rearrangements, accessory chromosomes and intron-rich genes can complicate genome assembly and the selection of cost-effective sequencing strategies. Here, we benchmark fungal genome assembly performance using simulated and empirical short- and long-reads datasets to evaluate how sequencing depth, assembler choice and genome characteristics influence contiguity, completeness, accuracy and computational requirements. Using simulated rea
papers.summary: This study benchmarks fungal genome assembly strategies by comparing short- and long-read sequencing data from both simulated and empirical datasets, evaluating how sequencing depth, assembler choice, and genome features affect assembly quality. The findings provide practical guidance for selecting cost-effective sequencing and assembly approaches for fungal genomes, which are often complicated by repeats and structural variations.

papers.title: Identification and Computational Analysis of BRCA1 Variants in Mexican Women from Jalisco, Mexico, with Breast and Ovarian Cancer.
papers.abstract: Breast and ovarian cancer are among the most common neoplasms in women, and germline variants in the BRCA1 gene markedly increase the risk of developing them. Despite existing studies, the frequency and spectrum of BRCA1 variants in women from Jalisco, Mexico, remain underexplored.
papers.summary: This study identifies and computationally analyzes BRCA1 gene variants in Mexican women from Jalisco with breast and ovarian cancer, addressing a gap in regional genetic data. The findings reveal the frequency and spectrum of BRCA1 variants in this population, which may inform local genetic screening and risk assessment.

papers.title: DNA Methylation Profiling in IDH-Mutant Gliomas: Biological Evolution, Molecular Grading and Clinical Implementation.
papers.abstract: Mutations in isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 or 2 (IDH1/2) define a major subgroup of adult-type diffuse gliomas and induce accumulation of D-2-hydroxyglutarate, resulting in extensive DNA and histone methylation changes. This epigenetic reprogramming underlies the glioma CpG island methylator phenotype (G-CIMP) and contributes to tumour lineage, differentiation state and clinical behaviour. DNA methylation profiling has consequently evolved from a research tool into an important ancillary method for CNS tumour classification, molecular subclassification and copy-number analysis. This narrative rev
papers.summary: This review discusses how DNA methylation profiling has become a key tool for classifying and understanding IDH-mutant gliomas, linking epigenetic changes to tumor behavior and clinical outcomes. It highlights the evolution from research to clinical application, including molecular grading and subclassification.

papers.title: Accurate detection of cholangiocarcinoma in primary sclerosing cholangitis using DNA methylation biomarkers in bile and plasma.
papers.abstract: Current methods for cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) detection in primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) lack accuracy, often leading to late, non-curative diagnoses. In this study, we aim at identifying DNA methylation biomarkers in liquid biopsies for earlier and more accurate CCA detection.
papers.summary: This study identifies DNA methylation biomarkers in bile and plasma that can accurately detect cholangiocarcinoma in patients with primary sclerosing cholangitis, potentially enabling earlier and more precise diagnosis compared to current methods.

papers.title: Genome-wide DNA methylation analysis of pediatric medulloblastomas from a Brazilian cohort: an exploratory study.
papers.abstract: DNA methylation profiling is a central tool for molecular classification of pediatric medulloblastoma. However, most reference datasets are derived from high-income countries, and the performance of established epigenetic markers in underrepresented populations remains insufficiently explored.
papers.journal: Clinical & translational oncology : official publication of the Federation of Spanish Oncology Societies and of the National Cancer Institute of Mexico
papers.summary: This exploratory study performs genome-wide DNA methylation analysis on pediatric medulloblastomas from a Brazilian cohort, assessing whether established epigenetic classification markers perform reliably in this underrepresented population. The findings provide initial evidence on the applicability of current methylation-based molecular subtyping in a Latin American context, highlighting potential differences or confirmations relative to high-income country reference datasets.

papers.title: Body Mass Index and Facial Aging: Mendelian Randomization and Exploratory Target Prioritization.
papers.abstract: Facial aging reflects genetic, metabolic, and environmental influences. Although obesity has been associated with older perceived facial age, the shared genetic basis and direction of the BMI-facial aging relationship remain uncertain.
papers.summary: This study used Mendelian randomization to investigate whether body mass index (BMI) causally influences facial aging, finding evidence for a causal relationship. It also prioritized potential therapeutic targets by exploring shared genetic pathways, suggesting that interventions affecting BMI could impact facial aging.

papers.title: The syntrophic network of pyrene degradation by the synthetic halophilic consortium PES.
papers.abstract: Owing to the high osmotic pressure, the degradation of high-molecular-weight polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (HMW-PAHs) in saline environments is quite difficult, leading to a scarcity of research on halophilic PAH-degrading bacteria. In this study, a halophilic synthetic consortium, PES, comprising Pelagerythrobacter sp. N7 and Salinicola sp. A11, was constructed on the basis of the bottom-up strategy. The syntrophic network for pyrene degradation by the consortium PES was investigated on the basis of genomic sequencing, functional gene annotation and expression, intermediates detection and
papers.summary: This study constructs a halophilic synthetic consortium (PES) from two bacterial strains and characterizes its syntrophic network for degrading pyrene, a high-molecular-weight polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon, in saline environments. By integrating genomic sequencing, gene expression analysis, and intermediate detection, the authors reveal how the two species cooperate to overcome the challenges of PAH degradation under high osmotic pressure.

papers.title: FastqCA: an effective FASTQ compressor through 2D spatial redundancy reduction.
papers.abstract: High-throughput sequencing generates vast amounts of FASTQ data, posing significant storage and transmission challenges. We propose FastqCA, a reference-free, cellular automaton-based compressor designed to exploit two-dimensional spatial redundancy across reads and positions. FastqCA applies a cellular automaton-based predictive-modeling algorithm to the nucleotide sequence stream in both modes, and to the Q4-quantised quality score stream in lossy mode. Evaluation against representative FASTQ compressors, including FQZcomp, DSRC2, fastqz, Scalce, Quip, NAF and SPRING, shows that FastqCA achi
papers.summary: FastqCA is a new reference-free FASTQ compressor that uses cellular automaton-based predictive modeling to exploit two-dimensional spatial redundancy across reads and positions. It achieves better compression ratios than existing tools like SPRING and NAF, especially in lossy mode with quantized quality scores, offering an effective solution for reducing storage and transmission costs of high-throughput sequencing data.

papers.title: Genomic sequencing of vineyard-isolated Bacillus strains and comparison with closely related Bacillus species reveals a putative new lineage, distinct pan-genome architecture and secondary metabolism potential.
papers.abstract: Bacillus species are ubiquitous in nature, and they display diverse traits of biotechnological importance, including the production of various enzymes and secondary metabolites. In this study, we profiled the genomes of vineyard-derived Bacillus strains shown to inhibit Botrytis cinerea mycelial growth and spore germination through the production of cyclic lipopeptides and cell wall-degrading enzymes.
papers.summary: This study sequenced and analyzed the genomes of vineyard-isolated Bacillus strains that inhibit the fungal pathogen Botrytis cinerea, revealing a putative new lineage with distinct pan-genome architecture and secondary metabolism potential. The findings highlight the biotechnological relevance of these strains for biocontrol and enzyme production.

papers.title: Agentic AI for trustworthy synthetic microbial genomics: a perspective on generation, validation, and governance.
papers.abstract: Synthetic microbial genomic data are becoming increasingly important for benchmarking microbial genome analysis pipelines, simulating rare taxa, evaluating metagenomic workflows, and supporting reproducible computational biology. Recent genomic foundation models demonstrate that biological sequences can be modelled at unprecedented scale, with emerging capacity for genome-level interpretation, generation, and design. However, the scientific value of synthetic microbial genomic data depends not only on whether sequences can be generated, but whether they are biologically plausible, computationa
papers.summary: This perspective article discusses the use of agentic AI for generating trustworthy synthetic microbial genomic data, emphasizing the need for biological plausibility, computational validation, and governance. It highlights the potential of genomic foundation models for genome-level generation and design, while addressing challenges in ensuring data quality and ethical oversight.

papers.title: rMAP-Candida: a modular Dockerized WDL/Cromwell workflow for reproducible Candida species typing, assembly-contiguity assessment, antifungal-resistance marker screening, and phylogenomic surveillance.
papers.abstract: Candida spp. infections are an increasing public health concern, particularly in settings where laboratory mycology, genomic surveillance infrastructure, and antifungal susceptibility testing remain limited. Accurate species identification, reproducible assembly assessment, conservative genomic screening for antifungal-resistance markers, and interpretable phylogenomic outputs are essential for surveillance and outbreak preparedness. However, fungal whole-genome sequencing workflows remain fragmented, difficult to reproduce across computing environments, and insufficiently adapted for implemen
papers.summary: This paper presents rMAP-Candida, a modular Dockerized WDL/Cromwell workflow that standardizes and simplifies whole-genome sequencing analysis for Candida species, including species typing, assembly quality assessment, antifungal-resistance marker screening, and phylogenomic surveillance. The workflow is designed to be reproducible across computing environments, addressing a critical gap in fungal genomics infrastructure, particularly for resource-limited settings.

papers.title: A circulating three-miRNA panel (hsa-miR-29b-3p, hsa-miR-19b-3p, hsa-miR-30e-5p) for early-stage ovarian cancer detection: a machine-learning bioinformatics approach.
papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer (OVCA) remains one of the most lethal gynecological malignancies, primarily due to late-stage diagnosis and the lack of reliable early-detection biomarkers. Circulating microRNAs (miRNAs) have emerged as promising non-invasive biomarkers for cancer detection and prognosis.
papers.summary: This study identifies a three-microRNA panel (hsa-miR-29b-3p, hsa-miR-19b-3p, hsa-miR-30e-5p) in blood that can detect early-stage ovarian cancer using a machine-learning approach. The panel offers a potential non-invasive biomarker strategy to improve early diagnosis of this deadly cancer.

papers.title: ProGenFixer: An Ultrafast and Accurate Tool for Correcting Prokaryotic Genome Sequences Using a Mapping-Free Algorithm.
papers.abstract: Although several tools exist for prokaryotic genome correction, most depend on external read mappers that impose computational overhead and usability barriers, leaving a need for fast, accurate, standalone solutions. We present ProGenFixer, a mapping-free tool that identifies and corrects errors in prokaryotic genomes using next-generation sequencing data. ProGenFixer compares k-mer profiles between an input genome and sequencing reads to pinpoint discrepancies, then applies a local assembly-based algorithm with a conservative correction strategy suited to refining high-quality reference genom
papers.summary: ProGenFixer is a new mapping-free tool that corrects errors in prokaryotic genome sequences using next-generation sequencing data. It compares k-mer profiles between the input genome and reads to identify discrepancies, then applies a local assembly-based algorithm with a conservative correction strategy, offering a fast and accurate standalone solution without external read mappers.

papers.title: Nanopore and EPIC array profiling unmask an atypical non-midline H3 K27-altered glioma: a case report.
papers.abstract: We report a rare case of Diffuse Midline Glioma, H3K27-altered, arising in a non-midline fronto-temporo-insular location in a 48-year-old adult, initially mimicking Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, based on radiology and histopathology. Integrated molecular diagnostics, including genome-wide DNA methylation profiling and Sanger sequencing, confirmed an H3.3 K27M mutation, while Nanopore-based methylation profiling provided a rapid and fully concordant classification, demonstrating the feasibility of real-time epigenomic diagnostics in clinical practice. H3K27M-mutant diffuse non-midline gliomas (DN
papers.summary: This case report describes a rare H3K27-altered diffuse glioma arising in a non-midline brain location in an adult, initially misdiagnosed as glioblastoma. Using Nanopore-based methylation profiling alongside standard methods, the authors achieved rapid and accurate molecular classification, highlighting the clinical utility of real-time epigenomic diagnostics for challenging glioma cases.

papers.title: Weighted epigenetic site correlation network analysis of chemotherapy impacts on osteosarcoma cancer survivors' male fertility, sperm, and endocrine parameters.
papers.abstract: The impacts of chemotherapy exposure on adolescent male osteosarcoma survivors as adults were investigated using a number of physiological parameters, with a focus on chemotherapy, reproduction, and sperm. The Children's Oncology Group (COG) clinical sites (protocol ALTE16C1) of previously collected and stored sperm samples were obtained for this analysis. The epigenetic DNA methylation alterations in sperm were assessed in 176 control adult male patients' sperm, and 183 chemotherapy-exposed osteosarcoma survivors' adult male sperm were provided by COG sites. The current study used a weighted
papers.summary: This study analyzed sperm DNA methylation in adult male survivors of adolescent osteosarcoma who had received chemotherapy, comparing them to controls. Using weighted epigenetic correlation network analysis, the authors identified methylation changes associated with chemotherapy exposure that may relate to fertility and endocrine parameters in survivors.

papers.title: Dietary sulforaphane in cancer chemoprevention: epigenetic regulation and PRMT5-MEP50 complex inhibition-a systematic review.
papers.abstract: Cancer chemoprevention using dietary bioactive compounds has emerged as a promising, cost-effective strategy to reduce global cancer incidence and mortality. Sulforaphane (SFN), an isothiocyanate abundant in cruciferous vegetables, has attracted considerable attention for its pleiotropic anticancer effects.
papers.summary: This systematic review examines the chemopreventive mechanisms of sulforaphane (SFN), a compound found in cruciferous vegetables, focusing on its epigenetic regulation and inhibition of the PRMT5-MEP50 complex. The findings support SFN's potential as a dietary strategy for cancer prevention through these molecular pathways.

papers.title: The TCN1 Paradox: Unraveling the Dual Role of Transcobalamin I in Colorectal Cancer-From Metabolic Regulation to Oncogenic Signaling.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a leading cause of cancer mortality. While genetic drivers are well-characterized, epigenetic alterations-particularly DNA methylation-are increasingly recognized as critical contributors. The vitamin B12 transporter Transcobalamin I (TCN1) has recently emerged as an epigenetically regulated gene with context-dependent oncogenic functions.
papers.summary: This review discusses the emerging dual role of Transcobalamin I (TCN1) in colorectal cancer, highlighting how its epigenetic regulation via DNA methylation can lead to context-dependent oncogenic functions beyond its traditional role as a vitamin B12 transporter. The authors propose that TCN1 may link metabolic regulation to oncogenic signaling, offering a new perspective on CRC pathogenesis.
